p: Ready to go up in the world? A few bits of prep will make the day smoother. Every climber needs a participation form filling in, and under-18s need a parent or guardian to sign it. It's easiest done online before you leave. Look at the age guidance when you book too, as there's usually a minimum age for climbers and rules about supervising younger children.
As for timing, allow a couple of hours all in. Arriving early gives you breathing space for harness fitting and the safety briefing, so the climbing time is all climbing.

Got a first-timer with the jitters? The best cure is a small, early let-go. Climb a metre or so, let go, feel how gently the auto-belay lowers you, and go again a little higher. It works on grown-ups as well as kids. Trainers, comfy clothes and a water bottle are all the kit you need.

There's lots around Ipswich to round off the day. Orwell Country Park, on the edge of town, has woodland and riverside walks with views of the Orwell Bridge. Jimmy's Farm, at Wherstead just south of the town, is a family favourite with animals, a nature trail and a restaurant. And football fans can always take a look at Portman Road, home of Ipswich Town. If you'd rather stay central, the Waterfront is lovely for a drink with a view of the boats.
